title.analysis: Authentic title "Pawn Shops are Seeing Something the Stock Market Isn't" uses an insider-signal frame: an unexpected observer (pawn shops) has information the market lacks. The script delivers on it with a "desperation spread" thesis (record pawn receivables versus record equity valuations) and then explicitly argues the other side (gold prices, mega-cap index composition), ending on "not a crash prediction". The title is curiosity-led but honest about the payoff. Its nearest peers are mostly personal-finance how-to titles; the two STRONG peers are a 2026 investing plan and a bonds explainer. Association only; no CTR or experiment evidence.

script.analysis: Full 16993 canonical characters read. A macro "two economies" essay framed by a narrative character (Jacob, an HVAC tech pawning tools) and a coined term ("desperation spread"). Structure: pawn mechanics and cost; pawn-company boom (FirstCash, EZCORP); asset-manager ownership; suburbanising pawn customer and a quoted Detroit pawnbroker; bank-branch closures; CAPE valuation and Fed constraints; K-shaped spending; stress indicators (saving rate, subprime auto, 401(k) hardship); Dollar General trade-down; a genuine counter-argument section (gold, mega-cap index composition, recession-call base rates); asymmetry thesis; signposts to watch; community/course pitch. Verified: FirstCash Q1 2026 revenue ($1.05B, +26%) and record $851M pawn receivables; EZCORP +46% revenue; record subprime auto delinquency above 2008; record Vanguard hardship withdrawals with eviction/medical reasons; Dollar General >$100K customer growth; 3.6% saving rate as originally published. Overstated or not supported: CAPE "near 43" (sources 40-41.6); bank branches "73,000" (FDIC June 2025 >76,000); EZCORP scrap "+64%" (sources +288% EZCORP, +161% FirstCash, so the gold confound is understated); the $160 starting loan size. Unverified: stock doubling, Vanguard 9%, FOMC dissents, household equity share, top-20% spending. The pawn-versus-card arithmetic reproduces (~243% versus ~24% APR). The stored ending is complete.
beat_map: Cold open: a pawn chain is one of the best-performing US stocks; Jacob pawns $3,000 of tools.
Pawn mechanics: loan not sale; $500 for 90 days costs ~$300 vs ~$30 on a card.
Why people use it: no credit check; 80-90% redemption; fees as recurring "plumbing".
Pawn boom: FirstCash $1B quarter, record $851M loans, stock doubled; EZCORP +46%; loan size $160 to $240.
Coined term "desperation spread"; Vanguard owns ~9% of FirstCash.
Customer shift: suburban, $60-100K households; Detroit pawnbroker "canary" quote.
Market valuation: CAPE near 43; record equity share; Fed constrained, record dissents, sub-6% mortgages.
K-shaped economy: top 20% spending; saving rate 3.6%; subprime auto past 2008; record 401(k) hardship withdrawals.
Dollar General trade-down from >$100K households; consumer staircase.
Counter-argument: gold drives pawn numbers (EZCORP scrap +64%); index is mega-cap tech; recession-call base rates.
Asymmetry thesis: no buffer, no backstop; market is a forecast, pawn counter a measurement.
Honest landing: not a crash prediction; Jacob's month-to-month margin.
Signposts: saving rate above 5-6% and cooling delinquencies vs below 3% and falling redemption; keep a buffer; subscribe close.

topic.analysis: Divergence between record equity valuations and rising lower-income household stress, using pawn-lender growth as the signal, with explicit gold and index-composition caveats.

topic.narrative_angle: The pawn counter measures the present; the market forecasts the future, and they disagree.
